Meccan. It has sixty-eight letters, fourteen words, and three verses.

Kamil ibn Ahmad informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Matar informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sharik narrated to us, saying:

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: Sallam ibn Sulaym narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Muslim, from his mother, from Abu Umamah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat ﴿وَالْعَصْرِ﴾ (By the Time), God will seal his life with patience, and he will be with the people of truth on the Day of Resurrection." [254] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/434.]]

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By the Time﴾ (wa-l-'asr): Ibn 'Abbas said: By time (al-dahr). Ibn Kaysan said: It is the night and the day, which are called "the two 'asrs" (al-'asran); the morning and the evening are likewise called "the two 'asrs". Humayd ibn Thawr said:

"The two 'asrs, a day and a night, will not delay, when they seek to reach what they have aimed for." [[Lisan al-'Arab: 4/576.]]

Al-Hasan said: It is the time after the sun passes its zenith until it sets. Qatadah said: It is the last hour of the hours of the day. Muqatil said: It is the 'Asr prayer, which is the middle prayer.

﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, for they are not in loss.

﴿and advise one another﴾ meaning they urge one another and each enjoins the other. ﴿to the truth﴾ meaning the Qur'an, according to al-Hasan and Qatadah. Muqatil said: to faith and the oneness of God (tawhid). It was also said: to acting upon the truth.

﴿and advise one another to patience﴾ in performing the obligatory duties and upholding the command of God. Ibn 'Awn related from Ibrahim, who said:

He meant that when a human being lives long in this world and grows old, he is in decline, weakness, and regression, except the believers, for their rewards are written for them, along with the good deeds they used to do in the time of their youth, strength, and health. This is like His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature; then We returned him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe﴾ [[Surat al-Tin: 4–6.]] to the end of the verse.

He said: ['Ali, may God be pleased with him, used to recite it thus:] "Indeed, mankind is in loss, and indeed he is in it until the end of time."

And likewise it is in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud.

'Ali used to recite it: "By the Time, and the misfortunes of time, indeed mankind is in loss, and indeed he is in it until the end of time." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/371, at the place of the verse.]]

The sound reading is that on which the general body of reciters and the codices (masahif) agree.

He recited: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. ﴿By the Time. Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, ﴿except those who believe﴾ Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, ﴿and advise one another to the truth﴾ 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, ﴿and advise one another to patience﴾ 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.
